newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tax estimate shows need for discipline -Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: Tax estimate shows need for discipline -Rexrodt.

text.p: The new estimate of an 18 billion mark ($10.6 billion) shortfall in German tax revenues this year underscores the need for greater efforts to consolidate the budget, Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Thursday.
Tax increases, on the other hand, would only lower the pressure for more disciplined budget-minding, jeopardising economic growth, corporate investment and jobs creation, Rexrodt said.
They would also burden private households, depressing domestic demand, he said.

"Instead of that, strict budget discipline is called for for the federal, state and local governments and the social security system. Clear and reliable tax structures are needed for growth and investment," Rexrodt said.
Eight billion marks of the 18 billion mark shortfall were already taken into consideration by the government's annual report on the economy, issued in January, he said.
The remainder can be dealt with through disciplined budgetary measures, he said.

Economic pressures are responsible only to a limited extent for the lower tax outlook, Rexrodt said. The government still expects 2.5 percent economic growth this year, and inflation appears more subdued than ever.
But labour market conditions are significantly worse than expected last fall, depressing income tax revenues.
The shortfall results to a great extent from the uncertainties of forecasting the effects of changes in tax law, and taxpayer behaviour, including tax evasion, he said.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.693 German Marks)
